newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-HOLE-IN-ONE HELPS SIGEL LEAD SENIOR TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HOLE-IN-ONE HELPS SIGEL LEAD SENIOR TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Jay Sigel aced the fifth hole Saturday as he opened up a three-stroke lead after three rounds of the $1.6 million, season-ending Senior Tour Championship at The Dunes Golf & Beach Club.
Sigel, who shared the lead after 36 holes, used a 6-iron on the 173-yard, par-3 to record the hole-in-one that helped him post a three-under-par 69.
Sigel stood at nine-under-par 207, three shots better than New Zealander Bob Charles. The 60-year-old Charles, who won the Kaanapali Classic two weeks ago, shot 71.
Kermit Zarley was in alone in third place at four-under 212 after firing a 69. Vicente Fernandez, John Bland, Mike Hill and Jim Dent were another shot away at 213, six shots off the pace.

Fernandez, who began the round tied with Sigel and Frank Conner, struggled to a 75, while Hill, a two-time champion at this event, posted a 74. South African Bland, who has won four times this season, posted a 72, while Dent shot 70.
Defending champion Jim Colbert, who leads the tour with five wins this year, was tied with Raymond Floyd and Conner at 214.
Lee Trevino, who won a five-way playoff last week at the Emerald Coast Classic, struggled to a 78 for 221.
The top 31 players on the tour money list are playing in the season-ending event, which will determine the Arnold Palmer Award given to the season's top money winner.
Hale Irwin topped the money list with earnings of more than $1.5 million entering this event -- some $66,000 better than Colbert. Irwin shot a third-round 76 for 218.
First prize for the 72-hole tournament is $280,000.
